releases.name: Mebular v0.3.4
releases.body: [English](#english) · [中文](#zh-cn) # Mebular v0.3.4 — Console settings refresh Console settings release. It refreshes the Console settings experience added around 0.3 without changing the 29-tool MCP surface, graph/event/sync formats, host adapters or stored data. There is no migration. ### Added - **Settings v2 shell** — a 760×720 settings modal (760×680 for About device) with a 160px left rail on desktop, a horizontal tab strip at 900px and below, and a full-screen layout on narrow screens. The six sections are General, Security, Memory, Integrations, MCP and Advanced; About device is a separate entry. - **Memory and integration IA** — the Memory section now owns the memory mode, model source, runtime status and model status; Integrations owns Agent configuration. Memory mode is a compact segmented control, with long explanations kept out of the layout. - **Consistent settings rows** — 40/58px row templates, a 150/1fr/68 field grid, 27px controls, grouped panels, three 114px security cards, always-visible configured/effective/ reason warning rows, and an About device page with three groups and three folds. - **Responsive, accessible and bilingual coverage** — layout baselines at 1440/1024/900/390, English and Chinese copy, reduced-motion behavior, settings deep links, fixed-position service menu, focus return, and expanded Console UI smoke assertions. - **CI reliability** — Windows-only bounded test retries, a slower local sidecar health probe, a regression test for delayed health responses, and retry-safe Windows temp-file cleanup. These are test/infrastructure changes, not new product capabilities. ### Changed - Settings tabs now use **集成 / Integrations** (formerly AI 助手 / Assistants) and **记忆 / Memory** (formerly 记忆运行时 / runtime), while the underlying agent and runtime configuration remains compatible. - The settings shell no longer scrolls as a whole: the header and rail stay fixed and only the content column scrolls. Rows remain single-line at 900px and stack cleanly on mobile. - Routine settings hints are carried by group/control `title` text; only actionable warnings, pending restarts and security exceptions stay visible in the layout. - The public MCP tool count, CLI commands, graph/event/sync formats and data layout are unchanged. This is a Console-only release. ### Fixed - **Settings tab overflow** — the expanded English tab set no longer overflows the settings strip by 5px at 1440/1024. - **Truthful dormant states** — sidecar tests accept `mcp/degraded` when a clean drain cannot be confirmed, while still asserting no new writes, no outbox flush, `409 mode_mismatch` and correct resume behavior. - **Slow-health false 503s** — a 200ms local health probe could mark a busy sidecar unavailable; the timeout is now 1000ms and covered by a 300ms regression test. - **Windows cleanup races** — provisioning harness cleanup is bounded-retry and best-effort, so a transient file lock no longer fails the suite; Windows timing-sensitive tests retry at most twice while persistent failures still fail. - **Settings smoke assertions** — aligned with the current IA (`Integrations`, `Add agent`, active tab order) and the updated security/about layout. ### Verification - Main CI run `43376114600` passed Linux build/test/lint (including Console UI smoke), Windows build/test/lint, DSH E2E, desktop smoke, semantic recall and WAN NAT. - Packaging dry-run run `43377170059` passed verify, the eight npm tarballs, Hermes bundle, macOS/Windows/Linux desktop builds and the full DSH E2E matrix. Publish, visibility and GitHub Release were correctly skipped; no registry or Release mutation occurred. - `verify:console` passed; the headless Console UI smoke covers the settings v2 layout, security cards, About device, responsive breakpoints, bilingual copy and reduced motion. - The formal `release/v0.3.4` run reruns the same gate before publishing. releases.name: Mebular v0.3.2
releases.body: [English](#english) · [中文](#zh-cn) # Mebular v0.3.2 — Memory Runtime stability + Fleet orchestration Mebular v0.3.2 is the stability release for Memory Runtime, with Fleet black-box orchestration included. The public MCP surface stays at **29 tools**, and graph/event/sync formats are unchanged. There is no data migration. ## Highlights - **Memory Runtime lifecycle** — managed, attached and manual sidecars now have explicit ownership and disable semantics. Attached/manual processes are never killed or replaced by Mebular; an unclean disable is reported as `degraded / disable_incomplete`, not a fake `stopped`. - **Data lifecycle and privacy** — staging, details, outbox, logs and remote-model requests use one minimization/redaction policy. Details follow role/kind retention (`conversation` 30 days, `tool_output` 7 days, `document_slice` 90 days, explicit `pinned`), with bounded idle cleanup and evidence-aware association. - **Honest state model** — `accepted`, `pending`, `queued`, `committed`, `failed`, `dead` and `degraded` are distinct. HTTP 202 and outbox acceptance are never rendered as graph commits; partial writes are reported as partial. - **Offline recovery** — stable idempotency keys survive restarts; ambiguous timeouts require authoritative readback; offline Compact no longer writes a title-only placeholder; Checkpoint high-water, `expectedRevision`, pending views and same-domain evidence validation are enforced. - **Host alignment** — DSH, Hermes and OpenCode/OpenChamber share the same pending/queued/committed, retry, mode-mismatch and checkpoint semantics, while keeping their documented host-specific limits. - **Operations** — sanitized JSONL logs, `mebular memory-runtime logs`, `doctor`, and `outbox list/show/rebuild/purge`. Diagnostics contain no tokens, message bodies or real home paths. - **Fleet orchestration** — capability/role cards, immutable plans, deterministic materialization, executable routing, join/MR gates, unified executor/adapter layer and the loopback OpenChamber runner. ## Fixes - Capability idempotency is now **single-flight** for concurrent requests with the same composite key and body; this closes the timeout-retry duplicate-write race behind the original `10,023/10,000` 10k failure. - Recall now queries every canonical detail kind, so `tool_output` and `document_slice` details expand instead of incorrectly reporting `detail_pending_sync`. - MCP graceful close no longer force-closes an already-admitted HTTP request before it can answer, so the configuration rollback request can return the contract's `409`; long-lived connections are still closed at the bounded deadline. - DSH, Hermes and OpenCode no longer turn a 202/pending/queued response into a committed record or checkpoint. ## Verification - **Full Jest:** 307 suites passed / 1 skipped; **3,389 tests passed / 1 skipped**; 0 failed. - **Coverage:** statements 89.16%, branches 77.92%, functions 90.26%, lines 92.20%. - **Hosts:** DSH 115, Hermes 57, OpenCode 41 and OpenCode checkpoint-recovery 32 host E2E checks; DSH memory runtime 37/37; immersive journey 84/84. - **Scale:** 10,000 MemoryRecords + 10,000 details, 0 extras, 200/200 read samples, 100% sampled detail-expand coverage; 6/6 failure/interruption scenarios passed. - **Real model:** Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M on macOS x64 with a test-only mirror; official size/SHA-256 verified, llama.cpp b12017, non-degraded extract/summarize/planQuery. - **Release:** all eight npm packages are visible at `0.3.2`; the release workflow passed verify, DSH, macOS/Windows/Linux packaging and visibility gates. ## Compatibility - Public MCP tools remain **29**; no new public `runtime_*` tools. - No graph/event/sync format change and **no migration**; 0.2/0.3.0 IDs, namespaces, tags and event history remain valid. - The sequential **v0.3.0 → v0.3.2 → v0.3.0** single-home upgrade/rollback drill passed. - Run the same version on every device. releases.name: Mebular v0.3.0
releases.body:
Memory Runtime release. Mebular can now run recall, extraction, compaction and task
checkpoints for a host while keeping the same graph, signed events, sync and cloud.
The MCP surface stays compatible at 29 tools; every runtime capability is opt-in.

### Added

- **Memory Runtime sidecar** — a separate `@mebular/memory-runtime` process exposes `/memory-runtime/v1` (status, ingest, recall, context, checkpoints, compaction, self records, trace feedback and model orchestration). All durable writes go through the internal MCP capability API (`/internal/memory/v1`) into the existing graph and event log; no new event type or sync wire protocol is introduced.
- **Two access modes** — lightweight `mcp` (default) and immersive `immersive` (opt-in). Mode is device-local. Switching changes processing only: it does not migrate, copy, rewrite or delete nodes. Lightweight mode starts no sidecar, opens no sidecar port and creates no sidecar files.
- **Runtime object model** — `MemoryRecord` reuses existing entity/fact/episode/skill nodes; `Compact` is a derived graph summary with source IDs and stale detection; `ContextCheckpoint` has revisions and leases and always goes through capability; `SelfRecord` is shared per logical agent and hidden from ordinary queries. `RawChunk` and `RecallTrace` live only under `<home>/memory-runtime/`, never in the graph, events or sync.
- **Four model sources** — built-in `heuristic` rules (default, offline), curated local Qwen packs, host-provided `CandidateRecord`s, and one explicitly allowed OpenAI-compatible API. The runtime never reads host credentials, calls a host model or switches providers on its own; failures fall back to heuristic with `degraded` status and warnings.
- **Curated local Qwen** — Qwen3 8B as the default pack, 30B-A3B for high-end MoE, 14B for high quality and 4B for low-memory devices. Packs are downloaded and selected explicitly, verified by manifest/checksum, run through a loopback `llama-server`, and are never installed or updated silently. `mebular models list|status|install|import|select|remove|start|stop|test` manage them from the CLI.
- **Model credentials and API safety** — API keys are stored only as `env:`, `keychain:` or `file:` references; plaintext keys never enter config, graph metadata, events, logs, Console or status. URLs reject non-HTTPS endpoints (loopback HTTP excepted), userinfo and cloud-metadata addresses; file keys must be private.
- **Console Memory Runtime settings** — sidecar lifecycle, model source, curated pack download/selection, API configuration, raw capture, trace retention and local model status are available in Settings → 记忆运行时. Sidecar status, active model, degraded reasons and counts are exposed without secrets.
- **Internal-object governance** — `compact`, `context_checkpoint`, `self_record` and defensive `raw_chunk`/`recall_trace` are hidden from default `memory_*` results, graph traversal and the Console memory list; `includeInternal=1` is admin-only. `memory_delete`/`memory_archive` reject internal objects and leave them to capability admin endpoints.
- **DSH Memory Runtime bridge** — opt-in `memoryRuntime` with recall on the first step of a new human turn, batched event ingest with retries and idempotency, compaction checkpoints, optional tool hiding with a governance allowlist, and optional idle maintenance using the current DSH session model. When disabled it registers no listener, timer or request.
- **Hermes MemoryProvider and companion** — `integrations/hermes/mebular-memory` adds automatic recall and turn/compaction ingest to Hermes while leaving built-in `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` active and untouched. The optional `mebular-companion` uses Hermes `ctx.llm` to submit host candidates, separately from the single external-provider slot. The GitHub Release also ships `mebular-hermes-plugins-<version>.tar.gz` with `install.sh` (no PyPI; provider installed as `plugins/mebular`, existing directories backed up).

releases.name: Mebular v0.2.4
releases.body:
Agent adoption and Skill deployment release. All six npm packages and the desktop app
ship as `0.2.4`; no runtime protocol or data-format changes are included.

### Added

- **Skill as a deployment artifact** — `connectClient`, App initialization, daemon startup, `mebular init`, and the `fleet --daemon` service path now ensure `mebular-memory` and `mebular-tasks` for detected clients. Installs include the `mcp/` fragments and a managed manifest.
- **Settings · Common “Auto repair”** — one-click, confirmed repair of detected assistant MCP entries and Skills. Failures are reported per client with redacted, expandable details.
- **All folder-based Agent targets** — OpenChamber/OpenCode, Hermes, Claude Code, Cursor and DeepSeek Harness each get their own detected global Skill directory; Claude Desktop remains a zip/UI upload flow.
- **Agent routing hints** — all 29 MCP tools now start their descriptions with “何时用”, and the MCP server publishes global `instructions` for routing and memory/task discipline.
- **SETUP runtime detection** — the agent playbook recognizes `runtime.json` + `/healthz` first, so an App runtime without a PATH CLI is not treated as uninstalled.

### Changed

- User-modified or unmarked Skills are preserved by default; only an explicit “Auto repair” force-overwrites the managed client assets.
- The locked settings page no longer duplicates “New cloud / Join cloud”; those actions stay in the top bar, while the settings page keeps diagnostics and guidance.
- Dependency maintenance: electron-builder and `@modelcontextprotocol/server` bumps.

### Fixed

- Managed-Skill cleanup now rejects absolute paths, drive letters, backslashes, empty segments, and `.`/`..` segments, preventing force repair from deleting files outside the Skill directory.
- `repair-api` Windows CI uses a real `.cmd` test double; `runtime.json` parsing no longer depends on Node being on PATH.

### Verified

- PR #288 required checks: 8/8 passed, including Windows, build/test/lint, desktop smoke, WAN NAT, semantic recall, and real DSH E2E minimum/latest/Node 22.
- PR #290 required checks: 8/8 passed; target matrix covers OpenChamber/OpenCode, Hermes, Claude Code, Cursor and DSH.
- Local gates for the target matrix: `verify:mcp:skill`, `check:docs`, `check:i18n`, and the target-matrix Jest suites.
- Packaging dry-run [run 40829880252](https://github.com/Windsander/Mebular/actions/runs/40829880252) passed: verify + 6 tarballs, macOS/Windows/Linux installers, and real DSH E2E minimum/latest/Node 22.
- Real Agent E2E: OpenCode 2.0.29 with DeepSeek Flash loaded `mebular-memory`, called `memory_write` and stored a preference; a new session then called `memory_query`/`memory_profile` and recalled it. Temporary HOME only; real user data untouched.
- App 0.2.4 packaged runtime boots and reports `0.2.4`; auto-install requires an initialized cloud and was validated through the packaged runtime + OpenCode path.

releases.name: Mebular v0.2.3
releases.body:
Identity-focused maintenance release. All six npm packages and the desktop app
ship as `0.2.3`; no runtime protocol or data-format changes are included.

### Changed

- **Identity contract** — `<storagePath>.identity.json` is now the sole authority for `deviceId` / `deviceName`. New configs write neither field, and all CLI, App, DSH and fleet read paths resolve the device identity from the identity file.
- **Transparent legacy recovery** — a valid identity with legacy `config.deviceId` / `deviceName` values is backed up to `config.json.identity-legacy.bak`, the stale fields are removed atomically, and startup continues without user interaction.
- **Shared preflight** — `init`, provision create/restore/join, and runtime startup use the same `home-identity` contract. Invalid or inconsistent identity is reported as `identity_invalid` / `identity_store_occupied` instead of an opaque `unreachable`.
- **No new App/DSH UI** — the common repair path is automatic; only an invalid identity fails closed.

### Fixed

- **`mebular init` identity handling** — an existing identity wins; conflicting `--device-id` is rejected; a root identity with a missing or invalid user master key now fails with `IDENTITY_TRUST_ROOT_MISSING` / `MASTER_KEY_INVALID` before touching config. Delegated identities do not require a root key.
- **No silent rekey** — a missing identity over a non-empty store fails with `IDENTITY_STORE_OCCUPIED`; an existing identity with a missing trust root fails closed and never generates a new master key.
- **Join safety** — `provisionJoinInto` and `fleet.joinWithToken` refuse to issue a new identity over existing store data.
- **Fleet and status consistency** — profile, fleet, admin and CLI status paths derive device identity from the identity file instead of legacy config fields.

### Verified

- Full Jest — **210 suites / 2153 tests passed**.
- Runtime coexistence — **13 scenarios / 153 checks passed**.
- Real DSH E2E — minimum, latest and Node 22 minimum passed.
- `verify:console` / `verify:onboarding` / `verify:daemon` / `verify:config` passed.
- Packaging dry-run — [run 40649283781](https://github.com/Windsander/Mebular/actions/runs/40649283781) passed: verify + 6 tarballs, macOS/Windows/Linux installers, and real DSH E2E minimum/latest/Node 22 minimum.
